proof_attempt_summary: Derived matching MSE order 1/(B+m) and honest connected-interval length order 1/sqrt(B+m) against every legal outcome-free adaptive membership audit, dependent assignment and original-record estimator; exact supplied-matching value and full-recovery elbow are credited to Hull. Mathematical review passed, the cited primary source was attested, and the independent terminal-validity gate confirmed subfield achievement with score ceiling 7.3 below the field floor 7.4; the specialized equal-size degree-one/noiseless-query scope and coarse constants prevent an in-scope field repair. No Lean/F-stage proof was attempted. Preserve the missing accepted-bank comparison and unconsumed duplicate interval theorem/support definition as non-load-bearing caveats; re-raise requires a deliberate new anchor or broader question.
tldr: For a single egocentric trial with unknown within-block perfect matchings, the sharp original-record minimax squared-error order is \((B+m)^{-1}\), and the uniformly honest connected-interval expected-length order is \((B+m)^{-1/2}\). Grouping or uniformly sampled gold memberships attains these orders. The converses permit arbitrary randomized adaptive audits, assignment dependence, labeled outcomes, and recorded seeds. With the true matching supplied, exact minimax risk equals Hull's finite-sample value \(\kappa_n\), attained by his nonlinear estimator under independent fair assignment. Singleton blocks and \(m\geq n-B\) recover that exact benchmark; these exact oracle identities are credited transfers of Hull's theorem. The new result is the scalable unknown-matching information frontier, including its consistency and oracle-improvement regimes.
gap: Network-menu robustness and known-graph minimax theory do not determine the value of buying exact membership information before treatment. A lower bound for arbitrary neighborhood interference does not apply to a smaller unknown one-mate class.
fill: An elementary computable frontier with matching original-record converses would price that choice throughout the public integer domain. A separate honest-length argument and oracle comparison make the result usable for prospective precision planning.
